findings.title: The new default forcing's synchronization cost is not priced by the audit meant to catch exactly this, and the one ledger row that models it was left numerically frozen while its own mechanism changed underneath it
findings.before: BASE: `elseif tag === :power  push!(syncs, Sync("ConstantPower band observable ($slot)", 0, HOST_SIDE_FORCING_SCALARS)) end` and the ledger row `(name = "adaptive dt, ConstantPower", cfg = (; adaptive_dt = true, velocity_forcing = :power), achieved = 2, floor = 1)` — correct at the time, because set_forcing_rate! fired once per step.
findings.after: HEAD adds a `:controller` branch and a `stages::Int = 1` parameter with the comment "`stages`... multiplies the readbacks of a STATE-DEPENDENT forcing, because such a forcing is evaluated at every stage rather than armed once per step... `ConstantPower` and `VarianceController` have rates that track the band observable" — yet the SYNC_LEDGER's ConstantPower row is left byte-identical: `achieved = 2, floor = 1`, built from a `cfg` that never sets `stages`, so `_syncs` silently falls back to `stages = 1` and reproduces the stale `2`. No SYNC_LEDGER row for `:controller` exists at all, even though `Simulation()`'s default velocity forcing is now `VarianceController` on the default 3-stage `IFLowStorageRK3`. The test `@test _achieved_syncs(syncs) == row.achieved` therefore certifies a number never recomputed for the new per-stage route, and the actual default configuration's sync cost (by the audit's own new model, roughly 1 + 3×2 = 7 crossings/step, not the 3 the docstrings still quote) is checked by no test.
findings.why_it_matters: This defeats the specific instrument CLAUDE.md's core invariant 4 (GPU-primary, minimal footprint/sync) and the optimality-audit discipline ("a recorded cost with no lower bound challenging it is an unexamined cost") exist to enforce: a change that plausibly tripled the default run's per-step blocking host readbacks shipped with the audit's own frozen number left untouched and the new default configuration entirely absent from the ledger, so the suite stays green while the regression class it exists to catch goes unmeasured.

findings.title: SimulationRun.jl's own docstring — the doc policy's designated "home" for this exact fact — still describes the default forcing as VarianceRescaling(over = :total) with an exact total-k guarantee, four times, after the default silently became a structurally different (band-target) forcing
findings.before: BASE (pre-rename): "By default the run is forced and stationary — a `BandRescaling` holds the whole-field kinetic energy at the value given by the `kinetic_energy` keyword (`over = :total`)", and the self-consistency note: "the choice is self-consistent only if the run really holds k at kinetic_energy, which the front door's `BandRescaling(over = :total)` guarantees and `:band` does not."
findings.after: HEAD: the SAME four passages (lines 93-96, 124-127, 169-173, 203-206) are only find/replaced to VarianceRescaling, e.g. "velocity_forcing defaults to a `VarianceRescaling` holding the total (whole-field) energy at the value given by the kinetic_energy keyword (over = :total)" and "...which the front door's `VarianceRescaling(over = :total)` guarantees..." — but the constructor now reads `velocity_forcing = d -> VarianceController(d; target = kinetic_energy)`. `VarianceController` has no `over` argument and its `target` is structurally the value of the forced band alone (`weighted_inner(field, forcing.band)` over shells 1-2 by default), the same quantity the retired `:band` mode held — not the whole-field value the docstring still claims is guaranteed.
findings.why_it_matters: A user reading Simulation's docstring — the single most-read surface in the package — is told the default run holds the total kinetic energy exactly at kinetic_energy, and that this is what makes the grid-mode viscosity choice (via Li2008) self-consistent. Neither is true of the actual default anymore: the docstring was renamed in place instead of rewritten to describe the new mechanism, so it now states a false-but-plausible physical guarantee about the package's single most common entry point.

findings.title: compute_audit.jl's per-forcing pass/transform-cost model was not updated for the ConstantPower rewrite or the new VarianceController tag, and the drift is invisible because only the OU tag is live-checked
findings.before: The `_forcing_pass_delta(tag, slot, scheme)` comment and `:power` branch describe ConstantPower via `set_forcing_rate!: weighted_inner(field, band) [field read] + rate .= a·indicator [indicator (real) read + rate write] + per-application rate reads`, returning `_ex(spectral_vector = 1, spectral_scalar = 1 + _applies(scheme), real_spectral_scalar = 1)`.

The only assertion this file makes against measured passes cross-checks `:ou` alone; `:power`'s frozen numbers are never compared to anything measured.
findings.why_it_matters: One of two sibling ledgers pricing the same op model (memory_audit.jl and compute_audit.jl) was updated for this round's Forcing.jl rewrite and the other was not, so the two now silently disagree about what ConstantPower costs, and VarianceController — the new default — has no representation in the compute ledger at all. This is the corpus's own named failure mode ("the sweep that skips its own surfaces"): the class fix was applied to Forcing.jl and to memory_audit.jl but not carried to compute_audit.jl.

findings.title: VarianceController's default relaxation-time formula hardcodes a dissipation-scaling constant that numerically contradicts the package's own calibrated Li2008 law used for the identical purpose two files away, while the adjacent comment asserts a test-pinning that does not exist
findings.before: (no prior formula — this is new code)
findings.after: `_stationary_dissipation_estimate(k, L) = 0.5 * k^(3 / 2) / (L / (2π))`, documented "ε_∞ ≈ C_ε k^{3/2}/L for a stationary box-filling flow. Spelled here rather than reached for from Phenomenology so this module keeps its independence; the constant is the same one that module fits, and the two are pinned against each other by a test." Algebraically this is ε ≈ π·k^{1.5}/L (0.5·2π ≈ 3.1416). Phenomenology.Scalings.Li2008's `stationary_dissipation(m, k, L) = (k/G)^{3/2}/L` with default G = 0.9 gives ε ≈ 1.171·k^{1.5}/L — a ratio of ≈2.68× between the two, independent of L. SimulationRun.jl's grid-mode viscosity solve calls `stationary_dissipation(Li2008(), kinetic_energy, side_length)` directly — the two formulas the comment claims are "the same" and "pinned against each other by a test" are neither: no test in test/ references _stationary_dissipation_estimate, relaxation_time, or turnover_time at all.
findings.why_it_matters: The controller's default turnover_time (hence its settling rate toward the target) is computed from a dissipation estimate ~2.68× larger than the estimate the SAME Simulation constructor uses, in the same file, to choose ν for the identical box — a category of error the project's own doc policy names explicitly ("a plausible 'X is just Y' equivalence... false until the expansion matches") and its comment falsely claims is guarded by a test, when none exists.

findings.title: The default `Simulation` silently stopped holding the whole-field kinetic energy — measured k settles ~30% above the requested value, while the docstring still promises `over = :total`
findings.before: velocity_forcing = d -> BandRescaling(d; target = kinetic_energy, over = :total),
findings.after: velocity_forcing = d -> VarianceController(d; target = kinetic_energy),
findings.why_it_matters: VarianceRescaling(over = :total) rescales the band to make the WHOLE-FIELD k equal `target`; VarianceController holds only the BAND variance. I ran the default run: at 32³/ν=0.03 to t≈67 the total k equilibrates at 1.88–2.05 (mean ≈1.95) against the requested `kinetic_energy = 1.5`, while k_band sits at 1.47–1.53. Every default run built since this commit reports a different u′, Re_λ and dissipation than the same call did at base. The prose was renamed, not rewritten, so it now states the opposite of the code in three places that survived the sweep verbatim: "a `VarianceRescaling` holds the whole-field kinetic energy at the value given by the `kinetic_energy` keyword (`over = :total`)"; "`velocity_forcing` defaults to a `VarianceRescaling` holding the total (whole-field) energy … (`over = :total`)"; and the grid-mode precondition "self-consistent only if the run really holds k at `kinetic_energy`, which the front door's `VarianceRescaling(over = :total)` guarantees" — a precondition the package's own default now violates (ε is off by (1.95/1.5)^{3/2} = 1.48×, so κ_max·η lands ~9% below its nominal design value). `kinetic_energy = 1.5 — the initial, and when forced the held, kinetic energy k` is likewise now false. The test that exists to exercise exactly this precondition, test/regressions/r4-edge-cases-06.jl, was renamed to `grid_mode_run(VarianceRescaling(target = 1.5, over = :total))` and left pointing at the retired forcing, so nothing measures the new default.

findings.title: The public `add_forcing_source!` hook changed arity 3→5 with no guard; a user forcing written to the base contract is silently never called

findings.after: add_forcing_source!(::AbstractForcing, N̂, field, domain::FixedDomain, diffusivity::Real) = N̂
findings.why_it_matters: `add_forcing_source!` is exported and documented as an extension point. findings.title: The VarianceController docstring's central claim — `dk_f/dt = -G(k_f - k_∞)/t_ℓ` exactly — names the wrong quantity; measured, the exact identity is on the TOTAL energy
findings.before: (new text)
findings.after: so that ``\\mathrm{d}k_f/\\mathrm{d}t = -G(k_f - k_\\infty)/t_\\ell`` exactly: the band variance\nrelaxes exponentially to a **stable attractor** with settling time ``t_\\ell/G``.
findings.why_it_matters: The code evaluates the restoring term and the denominator on the BAND variance but the numerator ε on the WHOLE field (`dissipation = 2 * factor * diffusivity * weighted_inner(field, domain.squared_wavenumber_kernel)`), so the identity that closes is d k_total/dt = −G(k_band − k_∞)/t_ℓ, not d k_f/dt. I measured both by finite difference at six times along a live run (32³, ν=0.03, gain 1, t_ℓ=1.08866): dk_total/dt matched the prediction to five significant figures at every sample (0.08353 vs 0.08353; 0.08089 vs 0.08089; 0.08003 vs 0.08004; 0.08070 vs 0.08070; 0.08259 vs 0.08260; 0.08544 vs 0.08544), while dk_band/dt ran +0.08923, +0.04219, +0.00126, −0.03287, −0.05983, −0.07966 against a predicted +0.080 — wrong in sign at three of six samples. Bassenne's derivation is exact for a whole-field forcing where the k in the numerator, the denominator and the error signal are the same k; restricting the forcing to a band and mixing the two breaks it. This matters because it is the documented reason to prefer the new default, and it is also the mechanism behind finding 1: the total energy is left as a free integrator, which is why it drifts to ≈1.95. Nothing in test/ asserts any controller property — the only VarianceController tests are a type check, an order check, and ledger rows.

findings.title: `_stationary_dissipation_estimate` is 2.68× off the estimate it claims to duplicate, and the test it claims pins them does not exist
findings.before: (new text)
findings.after:
# ε_∞ ≈ C_ε k^{3/2}/L for a stationary box-filling flow. Spelled here rather than reached for from
# `Phenomenology` so this module keeps its independence; the constant is the same one that module
# fits, and the two are pinned against each other by a test.
_stationary_dissipation_estimate(k, L) = 0.5 * k^(3 / 2) / (L / (2π))
findings.why_it_matters: The VarianceController docstring tells the user that the default `turnover_time` uses "``\\varepsilon_\\infty`` the stationary estimate for this box, the same estimate the grid-mode viscosity solve uses", and the comment adds "the constant is the same one that module fits, and the two are pinned against each other by a test". I evaluated both: `Forcing._stationary_dissipation_estimate(k, L)` against `stationary_dissipation(Li2008(), k, L)` — the function SimulationRun.jl:301 actually calls for grid mode — at (1.5, 2π), (0.5, 2π), (1.5, 1.0) and (3.0, 4π). The ratio is 2.6823 at every point (0.918559 vs 0.342447 at the default (1.5, 2π)); the local form divides by L/2π rather than L and carries C_ε = 0.5 rather than G^{-3/2}. So the default settling time of the package's new default forcing is 1.0887 where the documented basis gives 2.92 — 2.7× stiffer than advertised. Grepping test/ for `stationary_dissipation` returns only phenomenology.jl, simulation_run.jl and two regression files; nothing references `_stationary_dissipation_estimate`. The claimed pinning test does not exist, so the claim of agreement was never checked by anything.

findings.title: The front door's `over = :total` calibration constraint — a user-directed decision — was deleted by a one-line default change, and the docstring that promises it was left standing
findings.before: velocity_forcing = d -> BandRescaling(d; target = kinetic_energy, over = :total),
findings.after: velocity_forcing = d -> VarianceController(d; target = kinetic_energy),
findings.why_it_matters: `VarianceRescaling(over = :total)` was not a preference: ARCHITECTURE decision 54 records it as user-directed, and the grid-mode viscosity solve is self-consistent ONLY if the run really holds the whole-field k at the assumed `kinetic_energy`. `VarianceController` holds a DIFFERENT quantity — `band_variance = factor * weighted_inner(field, forcing.band)`, the shells 1-2 band alone. I ran the default 32^3 run for 2000 steps: k_band sits at 1.4744-1.5215 (the target) while k_total settles at 1.6165-1.6942, ~11% above the 1.5 from which nu was solved, and drifting rather than pinned. Every default `Simulation` therefore now runs at a different Reynolds number, a different u', and a different kappa_max*eta than the one it logs — silently, because the four places the docstring states the contract were only renamed, not rewritten: '“By default the run is forced and stationary — a [`VarianceRescaling`] holds the whole-field kinetic energy … (`over = :total`)`”', '“`velocity_forcing` defaults to a `VarianceRescaling` holding the total (whole-field) energy”', '“`VarianceRescaling` is a deterministic clamp: it rescales the band every step”', and the grid-mode precondition '“the run really holds k at `kinetic_energy`, which the front door's `VarianceRescaling(over = :total)` guarantees and `:band` does not”'. The ARCHITECTURE decision-58 entry claims the constraint is 'unchanged, and the controller holds it to a tolerance rather than exactly' — that is wrong in kind, not in tolerance: the controller holds the band's variance, which is the `:band` mode the same paragraph says does NOT guarantee it. No test asserts the default run's k; the only surviving `≈ target` assertion (`kinetic_energy(sim.state.velocity_spectral) ≈ 0.8 rtol = 1e-3`) is on an explicitly-passed `VarianceRescaling`, so nothing would have caught this.

findings.title: `add_forcing_source!`'s arity change silently disables every user-written implementation, with no misdeclaration guard and the old signature still documented
findings.before: add_forcing_source!(::AbstractForcing, N̂, domain::FixedDomain) = N̂
findings.after: add_forcing_source!(::AbstractForcing, N̂, field, domain::FixedDomain, diffusivity::Real) = N̂
findings.why_it_matters: The call sites in src/Generator.jl now pass five arguments, so a strategy that implements the three-argument hook is no longer reachable: dispatch falls through to the do-nothing default and the forcing is applied exactly zero times, with no error at construction, at `prepare!`, at `step!`, or at `deposit!`. I built a forcing with `add_forcing_source!(f::MySource, N̂, domain::FixedDomain) = (f.calls += 1; N̂)` and ran two steps of a `Simulation`: 'hook calls after 2 steps = 0'. This is precisely the failure mode the module already refuses to tolerate on the sibling hook — src/Generator.jl still throws 'implements set_forcing_rate! but does not declare uses_steady_linear_rate … so it would be given no rate array to fill and would never be applied', backed by `_overrides_rate_hook`'s method-table probe. That probe is generic over the function; nothing was added for `add_forcing_source!`. Worse, the change did not touch the docstring, which at HEAD still reads '`add_forcing_source!(forcing, N̂, domain) -> N̂`' — and docs/docstring_shape.csv still freezes that line — so the public contract instructs a user to write the exact method that is now dead. `AbstractForcing`'s own docstring likewise still lists `add_forcing_source!` as one of four hooks 'all default to doing nothing', with no note that its signature moved. The two new parameters were needed only by `VarianceController` (which reads `diffusivity`); `ConstantPower` uses `field` and the diff's own `StochasticOU` method comments 'the stage field is not needed'.

findings.title: VarianceController's central formula is a category error: the exponential relaxation it derives governs the WHOLE-FIELD energy, not the band variance it names
findings.before: (new code — the corresponding base behaviour is `ConstantPower`, whose docstring makes no relaxation claim: "The rate ``A`` diverges as the band's own value goes to zero")

It is k_TOTAL that obeys the relaxation law, with the BAND error as the input signal; k_f itself relaxes only via whatever share of the injected energy stays in shells 1-2. So the advertised "settling time t_l/G" is not the band's settling time, and the `target` a user sets is reached by the band only asymptotically while the total floats to an uncontrolled level. findings.after: By default the run is **forced and stationary** — a [`VarianceRescaling`](@ref ...VarianceRescaling) holds the whole-field kinetic energy at the value given by the `kinetic_energy` keyword (`over = :total`) ... `velocity_forcing` defaults to a `VarianceRescaling` holding the total (whole-field) energy ...
